packs.title: Parks and New Perspectives
packs.promise: Find another Prague in a leaning facade, iron curves and changing park views.

q.s: Give a bank, water and a bridge your own words.
st: Choose three ingredients in one stopped view: the riverbank edge, an open patch of water and a built shape across or above it.
Make an original two-line sentence or three-mark composition. Let one part follow the bank and another interrupt it like a bridge.
Save your composition and one word for its pace. A written arrangement and drawing earn equal credit.

q.s: Collect curves in a park pavilion.
st: Find one curved iron detail, one straight support and one shape around a window.
Make three small original marks or descriptions. Leave the building and all fittings untouched.
Order the details from the one that feels most delicate to the one that feels strongest, and save the collection.

q.s: Gather three weights in a monument’s view.
st: Find a form in the horse-and-rider silhouette, one broad edge in the stone base and one open patch of sky.
Give each an original word or mark for its visual weight: heavy, light or somewhere between.
Save the three-part collection with one sentence about what anchors the view. Do not climb or touch the monument.

packs.title: Stone, Sky and Small Stories
packs.promise: Find your own Prague in a curve, a crossing and a few carefully chosen words.

q.s: Collect three ways a building dresses up an entrance.
st: Find a roomy public stopping place facing the Municipal House entrance, away from doors, café tables and tram tracks.
Look for a curved outline, a patch of mosaic colour and a sculpted detail. Find all three on the exterior without going inside.
Choose one word for each: perhaps sweeping, shimmering or watchful. Match each word to a specific shape you can point out.
Save your three-detail collection, with one detail you would have missed at walking speed.

q.s: Find the smaller shapes inside a famous skyline.
st: Choose a comfortable spot in the square where the two main Týn church towers rise above the nearer house fronts.
Find one tall point, a smaller repeated point and a dark opening. Keep your collection above street level.
Compare the two towers. Pick one resemblance and one detail that looks different from your viewpoint; the difference can be caused by overlap or shadow.
Record your three shapes and the comparison without needing to name an architectural style.

q.s: Let a small corner supply the start of a story.
st: Choose a comfortable public stopping place on Na Kampě, clear of doors, restaurant seating and the walking route.
Collect three visible ingredients: a wall colour, a window or roof shape and a patch of shade or sky.
Write a three-sentence imagined scene using those ingredients. Let a small object, rather than a real passer-by, be the centre of it.
Save the scene and name the three details you borrowed from the view.
